edits.content:
## Answer template (MANDATORY) and shape check
Before the answer tags write ONE short line, then the bare answer:
`Type: <noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line, or own fact> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly, is that kind of thing, is not a clue word, and fits one distinctive clue detail (team, number, size)>`
If the Check fails, choose a new candidate before answering. Then apply these shape rules to the final answer:
- HEAD NOUN OF 'this X' FIXES THE TYPE: 'a treaty signed in this Alpine city' -> the city, not the treaty; 'this caustic acid' -> the candidate must itself be an acid. If the filled-in blank is the wrong kind of thing, reject it.
- STRIP ECHOES: the answer never repeats a noun or phrase the clue already states, nor the clue's own 'this <noun>' label. Strike every clue word from the candidate and keep the remaining head: 'this vitamin' -> 'C' (not 'vitamin C'); 'A "hasty" dessert' -> 'pudding'; 'these exiles "of Poker Flat"' -> 'The Outcasts'; 'nicknamed this' (the Progressive party) -> 'Bull Moose' (not 'Bull Moose Party'); 'this funeral structure' -> 'Pyre'. 'One of these' with a common noun gets the plain noun, with no modifiers copied from passages. The Rule 4 head-noun exception applies only to slots like 'this empire' / 'this purchase', where the bare modifier alone cannot name the thing.
- CLUE ALREADY STATES PART OF A NAME ('this Beatle named Ringo', 'known by the first name Marilyn'): the answer is ONLY the missing part, not the full name. This overrides the 'first + last name' default.
- BARE 'TITLE + NAME' clue (only an office/ruler title plus a personal name, e.g. 'Prime Minister <Name>', 'Chancellor <Name>'): answer the ONE-WORD country, realm or organization that person heads. Take the country from the passages' 'X of <Country>' wording and give just the country. Never answer with a role phrase ('Queen of <Country>'), the title, or the name itself. A clue 'This <office>: "quote"' asks for the PERSON who said it (never a role phrase or a bare first name).
- 'these' / 'one of these' with named examples ('the oak & the maple are these'): answer the plain CATEGORY NOUN all the examples belong to ('Trees'), not a series, product set or exhibit named in a passage title.
- LIST OF CHARACTER NAMES (see Rule 1): answer the show/film/book TITLE shown in the passage headings, never a descriptive phrase that merely precedes the names.

edits.target: - DELETE-CLUE-WORDS TEST: before answering, strike from your candidate every specific word or phrase the clue already states, and keep only the remaining head. 'Bret Harte wrote about these exiles "of Poker Flat"' -> 'The Outcasts' (not 'The Outcasts of Poker Flat'). 'Robert La Follette called it the Progressive party, but it was nicknamed this' -> 'Bull Moose' (not 'Bull Moose Party'). 'This funeral structure' -> 'Pyre' (not 'funeral pyre', and not 'funeral boat', which echoes the clue's 'funeral' and ignores that the passages say 'funeral pyre').
